significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish that an "internal, decodable confidence estimate" has a trajectory whose saturation predicts when further reasoning will cease changing the answer, and does so better than output-token entropy; this is primarily a form-(iii) predictive coupling, plus a form-(i) representation claim. It establishes a consequential behavioral phenomenon, but not yet a definite mechanism: "which components write it" and whether it controls backtracking are posed as further questions rather than asserted causal conclusions. This would sharpen the difficulty-dependent compute-allocation problem highlighted by Snell et al.'s test-time-compute work and confidence-based early-exit research such as Schuster et al.'s CALM; a verified-false result would usefully rule out the proposed internal-confidence advantage, although it would not rule out other internal stopping signals. In the topic-substitution check, generic efficient mechanistic reasoning would not earn this score; the claim-specific saturation-to-stability coupling is what lifts it modestly above the obvious confidence-probe hypothesis.

reach.justification: The concrete handle is the rule to "halt when predicted confidence plateaus above a threshold," an ex-ante intervention that can avoid additional reasoning before its cost is incurred rather than merely explaining a completed failure. After re-extraction on another model, the claimed qualitative relation still predicts that confidence saturation should precede answer stabilization, but the confidence direction and threshold would require recalibration and the claim supplies no architecture-invariant quantitative law. Its asserted scope covers reasoning problems and difficulty levels, and the downstream user could be an inference-system practitioner allocating compute, although the stated risks of out-of-distribution miscalibration limit confident transfer across model families. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: the generic topic supplies no usable stopping handle, whereas the quoted plateau rule, lead time, and practitioner uptake do.
